data.name: Zacheus
data.gender_notes: Zacheus is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Hebrew word 'zak', meaning 'pure, righteous, or clean'. In the New Testament, Zacheus is a chief tax collector who, upon meeting Jesus, renounces his corrupt ways and becomes a follower. This name reflects the idea of a transformation from a small, insignificant life to a pure and righteous one. The name Zacheus carries the meaning “Little, Small” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Zacheus usually hope their child will grow to embody little, small and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Zacheus belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Little, Small.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Zacheus total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

in_hebrew.name: זכאי
in_hebrew.meaning: זכאי הוא צדיק ונקי מזעמה של אלוהים
in_hebrew.long_meaning: זכאי הוא שם עברי שפירושו 'צדיק', 'נקי' או 'זכאי לרחמי אלוהים'. השם נגזר מהשורש 'זכא' שפירושו 'להיות צדיק' או 'להיות נקי'. השם זכאי מוזכר בברית החדשה ככומר שהתעשר לאחר שפגש את ישוע (לוקס 19:1-10). השם משמש כעדות לכוחה של החסד והגאולה הנוצרית.

in_greek.name: Ζακχαῖος
in_greek.long_meaning: Ζακχαῖος είναι η ελληνική μορφή του ονόματος που σημαίνει 'δικαίος' ή 'καθαρός'. Το όνομα προέρχεται από το εβραϊκό 'זכאי' και αναφέρεται στο Ζακχαῖος που ήταν ο πλούσιος δημότης που συνάντησε τον Ιησού (Λουκάς 19:1-10). Το όνομα έχει μεγάλη σημασία στην παράδοση της Εκκλησίας ως σύμβολο της μεταστροφής και της σωτηρίας.

in_latin.name: Zachaeus
in_latin.long_meaning: Zachaeus est nomen Latinum derivatum ex Graeco 'Ζακχαῖος', quod significat 'iustus' vel 'mundus'. Nomen Zachaeus in Ecclesia primitiva erat symbolum conversionis et salvationis, secundum narrationem Lucae (19:1-10). Nomen habet profundam significationem spiritualem in traditione Christiana.

in_english.name: Zacheus
in_english.long_meaning: Zacheus is a Christian name derived from the Hebrew 'זכאי' (Zakai) and Greek 'Ζακχαῖος' (Zakchaios), meaning 'righteous', 'pure', or 'God remembers'. The name is famously associated with Zacchaeus, the wealthy tax collector who repented and met Jesus (Luke 19:1-10). In Christian tradition, Zacheus symbolizes redemption, humility, and spiritual awakening. The name conveys a sense of moral integrity and divine favor.

data.cultural_impact: Named after a biblical figure, Zacheus is a name with strong associations to Christianity. Its origin suggests a person who, like the biblical character, was once lost but then found redemption and a new path in life. This name could inspire those who have had a transformation or who are seeking one. It also carries a touch of exclusivity, as it is not a common name.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Zacheus holds great spiritual significance as it represents the idea of transformation and renewal. It reminds us of the power of redemption and how even the most flawed or lost among us can turn our lives around and find a new path to righteousness. The name also inspires us to continually strive towards purity and righteousness in our own lives. Also, in the Christian faith, Zacheus' story shows that no one is beyond God's reach, and that all are welcome and valued in His kingdom.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Zacheus, a tax collector, represents transformation. He climbed a sycamore tree to see Jesus, symbolizing his desire for spiritual growth and seeking salvation. His renaming by Christ signifies a new beginning, leaving behind his past as a sinner.

biblical_reference.note: Zacchaeus, a tax collector, encounters Jesus and repents.

historical_references.reference: The New Testament book of Luke (19:1-10) recounts the story of Zacchaeus, a wealthy chief tax collector who wanted to see Jesus as He passed through Jericho. Zacchaeus, being short in stature, climbed a sycamore tree to get a better view. Jesus, noticing him, called him down and invited Himself to Zacchaeus' house for dinner. As a result of this encounter, Zacchaeus repented of his sins and gave half of his possessions to the poor and made fourfold restitution to those he had defrauded.

The Jewish Talmud, written in the 3rd and 6th centuries AD, refers to a man named Zacchaios, but it is unclear whether this is the same Zacchaeus mentioned in the New Testament. According to the Talmud, Zacchaios was a descendant of the high priest Jehoiada, and was a wealthy and influential man in Jerusalem who built a new gate for the Temple.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Zacheus is of biblical origin and is commonly associated with the parable of the tax collector in the New Testament of the Bible. In modern contexts, Zacheus is often depicted in art and literature as a symbol of redemption and spiritual growth, particularly in Christian communities. On social media, there are various groups and pages dedicated to exploring the story of Zacheus and its relevance to contemporary spirituality. In literature, Zacheus is a recurring character in Christian fiction, often portrayed as a model of repentance and faith. In visual arts, the story of Zacheus is depicted in paintings, sculptures, and other forms of art, further amplifying its impact and relevance in modern culture.

name_in_real_life.story: Michael Zacheus, a minister in New York, United States, shares that their name Zacheus meaning "Little, Small" has been a constant source of inspiration, guiding them to serve others and live according to Christian values.
